header:
Date: 2026-03-30
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Redwood: Avery Chen (AE), Marcus Li (SE)
Finexa: Sofia Martinez (Head of Privacy), Liam O'Connor (Platform Engineer), Nora Patel (Compliance Counsel)
transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll just do quick intros. I'm Avery, AE on Redwood Inference. Marcus is our SE.
[00:10] Sofia Martinez: Hi all, Sofia here. We're primarily concerned about data residency and region pinning for our EU customers.
[00:18] Marcus Li: Hey Sofia, yeah thanks. Quick agenda: SOC2/ISO docs, region pinning model and logs, cross-border processing, sub-processors and KMS options.
[00:27] Liam O'Connor: Quick context — Finexa is processing EU personal data and we need assurance that model inference and logs don't leave EU for certain endpoints.
[00:35] Nora Patel: Also need to know about contractual language — do you support SCCs, and what about subprocessors that may be US-based?
[00:43] Marcus Li: Sure. At a high level Redwood supports three deployment modes — hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private (VPC/on-prem). For strict residency we recommend either Dedicated with region pinning or Private.
[00:57] Sofia Martinez: So hosted API — can we pin requests to EU-only compute and storage?
[01:04] Avery Chen: Yes, we have region routing policies. You can configure routes per customer or per route to pin to eu-west-1 type regions. By default hosted may route to nearest capacity but we can enforce a strict eu-only policy.
[01:18] Liam O'Connor: If EU capacity is saturated, is there an automatic fallback to US? That's a hard no for us.
[01:24] Marcus Li: Under standard hosted, there is a fallback chain for availability. For your case we can enable strict pinning — no cross-border fallback. That means if EU pool is out, requests will queue or error depending on your SLA choice. There's a configuration flag — we call it region_strict_mode in the console.
[01:39] Sofia Martinez: Okay, and what about logs and KV cache? We cannot have logs or cache egressing to US.
[01:46] Marcus Li: All telemetry, request logs, and KV cache can be pinned to the region as well. For dedicated and private, everything stays in the customer's region. For hosted strict pinning we ensure model compute, KV cache and logs are stored and processed in EU zones; we also support encrypted logs at rest.
[02:02] Nora Patel: About sub-processors — who are you using in EU? And are any of them US-based contractors who might access data?
[02:09] Avery Chen: Our primary cloud sub-processors are AWS and GCP (region-specific). We also use a CDN and monitoring providers; full sub-processor list is in our compliance pack. Most compute and storage for EU pinned workloads stays on EU provider infrastructure. Some support tools (e.g., analytics) may be US-hosted — we'll flag those on the sub-processor list.
[02:29] Liam O'Connor: And do you offer contractual commitments — SCCs or data processing addendums (DPAs)?
[02:34] Avery Chen: Yes, we provide a DPA and will include SCCs where required. Our legal team can add EPL clauses for EU data residency. We'll include specific wording to prevent cross-border processing for pinned routes.
[02:45] Sofia Martinez: Encryption — do you support customer-managed keys (CMK) or HSM for encrypting model artifacts and logs?
[02:52] Marcus Li: We support BYOK/KMS integration for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we provide a KMS integration option: customer-managed keys via supported cloud KMS (AWS KMS, Google KMS) or our HSM-backed KMS for enterprise. In strict hosted pinning we can require CMK that is scoped to EU region keys.
[03:10] Nora Patel: How about in-transit encryption and keys for model weights?
[03:14] Marcus Li: All in-transit between our control plane and compute is TLS 1.2+, and model weights are encrypted at rest. If you choose private deployment we can limit key lifecycle to your KMS.
[03:24] Liam O'Connor: There's also the question of caching — does the prefix cache or KV cache store any PII? We want to ensure caching doesn't leak.
[03:31] Marcus Li: It's configurable. You can disable prefix caching for PII routes, or set automatic scrubbing/redaction before cache. We also offer TTLs and encryption for cache entries, and you can store the cache only in EU zones.
[03:45] Sofia Martinez: What about retaining transcripts and audit logs for compliance — can retention be set per-account and per-region?
[03:51] Avery Chen: Yes, retention windows are configurable per tenant. You can set audit log retention to meet your retention policy. We also provide immutable append-only audit logs and export options to your storage accounts in EU.
[04:03] Nora Patel: For SOC2 and ISO evidence — can you share your reports and AICPA letter?
[04:08] Avery Chen: Absolutely, we'll attach SOC2 Type II report and ISO certs. We'll redact some details, but key control mappings are provided.
[04:15] Liam O'Connor: Are there any cases where data will be processed outside the EU beyond logs? For example metadata for billing or usage analytics.
[04:22] Marcus Li: Usage billing metadata — we can route billing events to either EU or US. For your case we can route billing processing to EU. Some internal analytics may still be US-based; we can opt you out or provide aggregated exports instead. We'll put that in the DPA.
[04:37] Sofia Martinez: How do you handle support escalations? Sometimes support engineers need to reproduce issues and need access to traces. Will that require data crossing borders?
[04:45] Marcus Li: We have role-based access controls and SSO integration. Support access can be restricted; we can provide EU-only support pool or limit redwood support engineers' access to sanitized data. For deeper debugging we can do session replay in EU if needed under strict access controls.
[04:59] Nora Patel: On SSO, do you support SAML/OIDC and can we enforce SCIM for user provisioning?
[05:04] Avery Chen: Yes we support SAML and OIDC, and SCIM-based provisioning. RBAC is customizable and integrates with your IdP.
[05:12] Liam O'Connor: Are audit logs correlated with token-level cost and latency traces? We need traceability for requests that processed EU personal data.
[05:19] Marcus Li: Yes, our console provides token-level breakdowns and per-request trace IDs. You can export these logs to your EU storage and retain them per your policy.
[05:30] [crosstalk] Sofia Martinez: Sorry, just to confirm — if we go hosted with strict pinning and the EU model variant is not available for a model, will Redwood automatically fall back to a smaller EU-compatible quantized model, or error out?
[05:44] Marcus Li: Good question. We have two configurable strategies: canary fallback to a compatible EU-hosted variant (e.g., quantized smaller model) or strict-no-fallback. Given your compliance needs, strict-no-fallback or automatic queueing is the safer config. If you want a seamless experience we can prepare an EU-compatible fallback model image in the dedicated pool.
[06:03] Sofia Martinez: About subprocessors again — who performs maintenance on the keys? Who has console access?
[06:09] Avery Chen: Key management depends on deployment. With CMK you control keys. With our managed KMS, access is restricted to a small ops team under tight audit. We'll provide the list of named individuals and processes in the compliance pack.
[06:21] Liam O'Connor: Do you have any certifications for data residency — e.g., data center contracts or guarantees from cloud providers?
[06:27] Marcus Li: We rely on cloud provider guarantees for physical data centers; we also have internal controls verifying region placement. For Dedicated and Private, we can supply architecture diagrams showing all components in EU.
[06:39] Nora Patel: Can you explain cross-border processing if a subprocessor needs to run a transient job in the US?
[06:45] Marcus Li: If any subprocessors perform processing outside EU, that will be listed and require explicit approval. For your DPA we can require prior consent for any cross-border subprocesses and notify you.
[06:56] Sofia Martinez: What about backups — are backups geo-replicated? If so, can we opt out of replication to non-EU regions?
[07:02] Marcus Li: Backups by default replicate within the same region. We do have optional geo-replication for disaster recovery; for your setting we will disable replication outside EU.
[07:11] Liam O'Connor: For on-prem/private deployments — does Redwood ship container images and do we manage the entire stack?
[07:16] Avery Chen: For Private we provide an appliance/container bundle, and you run in your VPC/on-prem. We provide support images and upgrade procedures; keys and logs stay with you.
[07:25] Sofia Martinez: A few micro items — do you support EU-only sub-processor lists in the contract?
[07:31] Avery Chen: Yes, we can include EU-only subprocessor commitments and require change notifications.
[07:36] [silence/typing]
[07:40] Marcus Li: I'll share a short diagram of the route: client -> eu ingress -> model compute (eu) -> kv cache (eu) -> logs (eu). If anything goes out of region it's controlled by strict flags.
[07:53] Liam O'Connor: One more question: what about model weights — are they stored in EU? If Redwood uses public/open models that you host, where are those artifacts?
[08:01] Marcus Li: For hosted pinned workloads we ensure model artifact hosting in EU buckets. If you bring-your-own-model (BYOM) we can ingest into EU-only storage and manage them under your key policy.
[08:12] Sofia Martinez: Are there any edge cases where human review might access data outside EU, like for safety escalations?
[08:19] Avery Chen: We have a documented safety escalation process. For accounts with EU-only requirements, human review is limited and must be done under EU-only controls or on redacted data unless you approve otherwise.
[08:31] Nora Patel: Can you map your controls to our auditors' questions — we'll want a table of controls vs description vs evidence.
[08:37] Avery Chen: Yes, that's in the compliance package — control mappings to SOC2/ISO clauses and evidence artifacts. We'll include that.
[08:45] Sofia Martinez: Great. For the pilot, we'd like to test EU-only strict pinning for two routes, capture audit logs and do a risk review. Timeline is next two weeks.
[08:54] Marcus Li: Sounds good. We'll prepare a pilot plan: configuration steps, test cases (latency, failover, access controls), and acceptance criteria.
[09:03] [30:00 mark — moderator note: call progressed into detailed config walk-throughs, snippets omitted for brevity]
[30:10] Marcus Li: (demo voice) In the console we set route.policy = "eu_strict" and enable cmk_eu_key_id. There's a toggle for allow_cross_border = false.
[30:24] Liam O'Connor: Can you show how logs export to our S3 in eu-west?
[30:29] Marcus Li: Yep, configure export.destination = "s3://finexa-eu-audit" and rotation/retention. We'll help with IAM role creation and least-privilege policy.
[30:42] Sofia Martinez: Is there a cost delta for strict pinning?
[30:45] Avery Chen: There's a small premium for reserved EU-only capacity and CMK usage, we'll provide pricing lines in the next email.
[30:53] Nora Patel: Any remaining questions?
[30:57] Liam O'Connor: Just to confirm fallback — we will choose strict-no-fallback and queue semantics for the pilot.
[31:03] Marcus Li: Noted. We'll implement queue behavior and surface metrics for queued/rate-limited requests.
[31:10] Ava (Speaker 1): um are there any limitations on model versions or quantization when pinned? Sometimes the latest model isn't available in all regions.
[31:18] Marcus Li: Correct, some variants may not be available in region. We'll map compatible model variants and propose an EU-hosted fallback image for the pilot.
[31:28] Sofia Martinez: Thanks — that addresses most concerns.
[31:31] Avery Chen: Recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO and sub-processor list, Marcus will share implementation guide and run a quick EU benchmark, Nora to share data flows, and we'll schedule pilot kickoff week of 2026-04-05.
[31:44] Nora Patel: Thanks everyone.
[31:46] Avery Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up in the doc and email.
[31:50] [call ends]

Note: transcription contains some small speech-to-text imperfections (e.g., "KV cash", "region_strict_mode" spelled inconsistently).
